Cultivating possession and payment of rent to the landholder supported the conclusion that the person was in possession as a tenant. The Court did not accept the appellant’s attempt to characterize his earlier tenancy proceedings as lacking jurisdiction on the basis of his newly advanced position.
members.conclusion: The appellant could not change his position and contend that tenancy law did not apply or that the other party was not his tenant; the other party’s possession and payment of rent were as a tenant.

predicates.challenge_to_tenancy_status_after_prior_: A party challenged the other person’s tenancy status after previously pursuing proceedings treating that person as a tenant.
predicates.inconsistent_litigation_position: The party advanced a position that contradicted the position it had maintained in earlier proceedings.
predicates.cultivating_possession_with_rent_paid: The other person cultivated the land and paid rent to the party claiming to be the landholder.

members.legal_issue: The prosecution cannot abandon the foundation of its case on appeal and seek to sustain the conviction on a new theory first advanced there.
material_facts: The prosecution's case rested on the claim that the accused intended to kill one person but mistakenly killed the deceased instead.
The State asked the Supreme Court to consider the evidence on a different hypothesis first presented before it.
The State's appeal challenged the High Court's acquittal.
members.legal_principle: A prosecution cannot ask the court to discard the very substratum of its case and construct a new theory founded on a hypothesis presented for the first time on appeal. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on.
members.conclusion: The Court rejected the State's request to discard the foundation of its case and construct a new theory on appeal.

predicates.state_appeal_from_acquittal: The State appealed a judgment acquitting the accused.
predicates.prosecution_case_has_foundational_theory: The prosecution presented a particular theory as the foundation of its case.
predicates.different_hypothesis_first_raised_on_app: The prosecution first advanced a different hypothesis on appeal.

members.legal_issue: A factual defence that was not pleaded and was admitted at trial cannot be raised for the first time at an appellate stage.
material_facts: The landlord pleaded that the sweetmeat business he wished to move to the disputed shop was his own business.
The tenants admitted that allegation in their written statement and did not contest it at trial.
No issue was framed and no evidence was led on whether the business belonged to a joint family.
The tenants first argued at a late appellate stage that the business belonged to the landlord’s joint family.
members.legal_principle: A claim or defence not put forward in the pleadings cannot be supported by evidence, and a new factual contention cannot be raised for the first time on appeal. The Court relied on Siddik Mahomed Shah v. Mt. Saran, Bhagat Singh v. Jaswant Singh, and Bachan Singh v. Dhian Dass.
members.conclusion: The new factual defence could not be entertained at the appellate stage.

rule.if: appellate_stage_in_eviction_case and business_ownership_admitted_in_pleadings and no_issue_or_evidence_on_ownership and new_factual_defence_first_raised_on_appeal

predicates.appellate_stage_in_eviction_case: The dispute is being considered at an appellate stage in an eviction case.
predicates.business_ownership_admitted_in_pleadings: The opposing party admitted in its pleadings that the business relied on for the eviction claim belonged to the claimant.
predicates.no_issue_or_evidence_on_ownership: No issue was framed and no evidence was presented on the disputed ownership of the business at trial.
predicates.new_factual_defence_first_raised_on_appe: A party first raised on appeal a factual defence about who owned the business.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot avoid the consequences of its pleaded position that disputed properties are trust properties by advancing an inconsistent contention for the first time on appeal.
material_facts: The defendants' written statement accepted that the properties listed in the plaint were covered by the trust and claimed that they had become trustees of those properties under the trust deed.
The defendants maintained that position before the trial court and the High Court.
On appeal, they argued that the trust deed covered only specified properties belonging to its settlors and not the other listed properties.
members.legal_principle: The court relied on the defendants' unequivocal written pleading and their consistent case in the lower courts, which accepted that the listed properties were covered by the trust. It did not accept the inconsistent contention newly advanced on appeal. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this holding.
members.conclusion: The court rejected the new contention and treated the properties listed in the plaint as covered by the trust for purposes of the dispute.

predicates.appeal_in_trust_property_dispute: The proceeding is an appeal in a dispute about whether identified properties are held on trust.
predicates.prior_pleading_admitted_property_coverag: A party's earlier pleading accepted that the disputed properties were covered by the trust.
predicates.prior_case_claimed_trusteeship_over_thos: The party maintained in the lower courts that it held the properties as trustee under the trust instrument.
predicates.appellate_argument_contradicts_prior_pos: On appeal, the party advanced a claim about the properties that contradicted its earlier pleaded and maintained position.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot rely on acquiescence as a ground to defeat a claim when that ground was not pleaded and no issue on it was framed.
material_facts: A party argued that a signatory had acquiesced in a division of property by signing the instrument and not challenging it for a period of years.
The party had not pleaded acquiescence, and the trial court had framed no issue on it.
members.legal_principle: A party may not obtain a decision on a factual plea that was neither raised in the pleadings nor made an issue for trial.
members.conclusion: The party could not set up the plea of acquiescence, and the finding that the signatory had relinquished her share on that basis was erroneous.

predicates.partition_proceeding: The parties were litigating a division of jointly held family property.
predicates.acquiescence_raised_without_pleading: A party argued that another party had accepted a property division by conduct, although the argument had not been pleaded.
predicates.no_issue_framed_on_acquiescence: The court did not frame an issue for trial on whether the alleged conduct amounted to acquiescence.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot obtain relief on a materially new case raised on appeal when the case was not advanced at trial and the opposing party had no opportunity to meet it.
material_facts: At trial, the beneficiary claimed that she acquired the property with her personal funds; the opposing party contended that waqf funds paid for it.

In the High Court, the beneficiary advanced a different case based on her husband’s personal funds, and in the Supreme Court she argued that waqf income used for the acquisition had become her personal money.
The parties had adduced evidence and tried the case on the source of the acquisition funds, not on the new theory advanced in the Supreme Court.
members.legal_principle: Pleadings are construed in light of the stand taken at trial and the issues on which the parties adduced evidence and argued. Relief cannot ordinarily be granted on a case that had no foundation in the pleadings and that the opposing party was not called on to meet. The Court distinguished Srinivas Ram Kumar v. Mahabir Prasad, Nagubai Ammal v. B. Shama Rao and Kunju Kesavan v. M. M. Philip, where the opposing party had admitted, raised, or tried the alternative matter and was not prejudiced by its consideration.
members.conclusion: The beneficiary could not rely on the new theory in the Supreme Court, and it did not provide a basis for granting her claim.

rule.if: civil_appeal and appellant_raises_new_material_case and case_not_tried_on_that_basis and opposing_party_had_no_opportunity_to_meet_it

predicates.civil_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a civil dispute.
predicates.appellant_raises_new_material_case: The appellant advances on appeal a materially different factual or legal basis for the requested relief.
predicates.case_not_tried_on_that_basis: The parties did not adduce evidence or conduct the trial on the basis of that new case.
predicates.opposing_party_had_no_opportunity_to_mee: The opposing party was not called on during the trial to answer the new case.

members.legal_issue: Evidence of a source of title that was not pleaded cannot be relied on to establish title when the opposing party had no opportunity to meet that case.
material_facts: The plaintiff's pleaded case was that the predecessor in title acquired the property by inheritance.
The plaintiff relied on an earlier sale deed to establish a different source of the predecessor's title, although that source had not been pleaded.
The plaintiff admitted that the deed had not been disclosed in the plaint, and the amendment application seeking new pleadings was rejected by the first appellate court.
members.legal_principle: A party must plead the source of title on which the claim is based. Without that pleading, the opposing party has no opportunity to rebut the case, and evidence concerning the unpleaded source cannot be relied on to establish title. The judgment cites no earlier case for this principle.
members.conclusion: The courts below rightly declined to rely on the unpleaded deed to establish the plaintiff's title.

predicates.civil_title_suit: The plaintiff brought a civil suit to establish title to property.
predicates.title_source_not_pleaded: The plaintiff did not plead the source of title later relied on to establish ownership.
predicates.evidence_of_unpleaded_title_source_intro: The plaintiff introduced evidence concerning that unpleaded source of title.

members.legal_issue: A court cannot find that subletting occurred at a particular time when that timing was not pleaded and no issue on it was framed.
material_facts: The plaint did not state when the tenant sublet the two shops.
No pleading or issue addressed the date of subletting.
The High Court found that the subletting occurred after the relevant rent-control order came into force.
members.legal_principle: A factual finding on a matter not pleaded and not made an issue cannot be supplied by the court. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this procedural point.
members.conclusion: The High Court erred in finding that the subletting occurred after the rent-control order came into force; on the record, the Court could conclude only that it occurred sometime after the later shops were let.

predicates.second_appeal: The matter is an appeal from a decision made in second appeal.
predicates.subletting_date_not_pleaded: The pleadings do not state when the subletting occurred.
predicates.no_issue_on_subletting_date: No issue was framed for trial on when the subletting occurred.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot establish a sub-tenancy defense through evidence when the defense was not pleaded and no issue on it was framed.
material_facts: The written statement did not plead the alleged sub-tenancy with material particulars, and no issue on sub-tenancy was framed.
The sub-tenancy argument was advanced at the appellate stage and relied on revenue entries.
The witnesses said to have the best knowledge of the alleged arrangement were not produced to testify.
members.legal_principle: In a civil suit, evidence relating to a matter cannot be considered to build a case that was not pleaded; a properly pleaded matter may be made an issue for determination. The judgment states this as settled law but cites no earlier case.
members.conclusion: The sub-tenancy argument could not be relied on and was rejected as devoid of merit.

predicates.civil_suit: The matter is being determined in a civil suit.
predicates.subtenancy_defense_not_pleaded: The party did not plead the alleged sub-tenancy in its written case.
predicates.subtenancy_issue_not_framed: The court did not frame an issue for determination on the alleged sub-tenancy.

members.legal_issue: A new ground for eviction that was not pleaded or raised in the trial court or first appeal cannot be introduced for the first time in a second appeal.
material_facts: The landlord had not pleaded the change-of-purpose ground in the plaint.
No issue on that ground was framed, and the ground was not urged before either the trial court or the first appellate court.
The landlord raised the ground for the first time in the High Court in second appeal.
members.legal_principle: The Court held that raising this ground for the first time in second appeal was impermissible where it had not been pleaded, made the subject of an issue, or urged in the lower courts. No specific statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this procedural conclusion.
members.conclusion: The High Court should not have entertained the new eviction ground in the second appeal.

rule.if: second_appeal_in_eviction_proceeding and ground_absent_from_pleadings and no_issue_on_ground and ground_not_raised_in_lower_courts

predicates.second_appeal_in_eviction_proceeding: The matter is a second appeal in an eviction proceeding.
predicates.ground_absent_from_pleadings: The party seeking eviction did not include the ground in the initiating pleading.
predicates.no_issue_on_ground: The lower court did not frame an issue on that ground.
predicates.ground_not_raised_in_lower_courts: The party did not urge that ground before the trial court or first appellate court.

members.legal_issue: A court cannot decide a dispute on a factual issue that the parties did not raise in their pleadings or on which no issue was framed for trial.
material_facts: The defendant denied the purchaser’s title and claimed ownership by adverse possession in his written statement, but did not claim that he occupied the shop as a tenant.
Because tenancy was not pleaded, the trial court framed no issue on tenancy and neither lower court made a finding on it.
The High Court nevertheless held that the defendant was a tenant and that possession had to be pursued through a tenancy claim.
members.legal_principle: Parties cannot travel beyond their pleadings, and a court must decide the issues arising from those pleadings. A finding on an issue de hors the pleadings is without jurisdiction. The judgment cites no particular provision or earlier case for this principle.
members.conclusion: The High Court’s tenancy finding was outside the pleadings and was not a proper basis for setting aside the lower courts’ decrees.

rule.if: civil_possession_case and tenancy_not_pleaded and no_tenancy_issue_framed and court_decided_tenancy

predicates.civil_possession_case: The proceeding is a civil dispute seeking possession of property.
predicates.tenancy_not_pleaded: The party said to be a tenant did not plead that a tenancy existed.
predicates.no_tenancy_issue_framed: The trial court framed no issue for determination about tenancy.
predicates.court_decided_tenancy: A court decided that the occupant held the property as a tenant.

members.legal_issue: An appellate court cannot decide a case on a new factual basis that was not pleaded and would require fresh evidence.
material_facts: The respondents’ pleaded case was that they had obtained the lands from the lessor from the outset.

The High Court also treated the respondents as having obtained, or being deemed to have obtained, a new tenancy after the lessee’s lease expired, although that case had not been pleaded and required further evidence.
Evidence indicated that new settlement forms had not been issued after the lease expired.
members.legal_principle: A court in appeal cannot construct a new case for a party and decide it on a ground that was not pleaded, particularly where the ground requires fresh evidence or material.
members.conclusion: The High Court erred in deciding the case on the unpleaded basis of a new post-expiry tenancy.

predicates.appellate_civil_appeal: A party appealed from a civil decree that had been reversed by a higher court.
predicates.unpleaded_new_factual_basis: A court relied on a factual basis that the party relying on it had not pleaded.
predicates.basis_requires_fresh_evidence: Deciding the new factual basis would require evidence or material not already before the court.

members.legal_issue: A party may not introduce an appellate ground that depends on factual matters when those matters were not pleaded and would require evidence or factual inquiry.
material_facts: The appellant did not refer to the nationalisation legislation in its written statement, and no issue or argument on its effect was raised before the trial court, appellate court, or revisional court.

The appellant sought to raise the point for the first time before the Supreme Court without amending its pleadings; its claim that it acted as the Central Government’s agent depended on facts that had not been pleaded or proved.
members.legal_principle: Relief should ordinarily not be granted on a ground outside the pleadings, and evidence cannot be relied on where it is not supported by pleadings. Material facts must be pleaded and proved, and a matter should not ordinarily be decided without an issue having been framed. A new pure legal ground requiring no inquiry or proof may be raised at any stage, but a new factual case requires amendment of the pleadings. The Court relied on M/s. Trojan & Co. v. R.M.N.N. Nagappa Chettiar, State of Maharashtra v. Hindustan Construction Company Ltd., Kalyan Singh Chouhan v. C.P. Joshi, Ram Sarup Gupta v. Bishun Narain Inter College, Bachhaj Nahar v. Nilima Mandal, Kashi Nath v. Jaganath, Biswanath Agarwalla v. Sabitri Bera, Syed and Company v. State of Jammu & Kashmir, Chinta Lingam v. Government of India, J. Jermons v. Aliammal, M/s. Sanghvi Reconditioners Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India, and Greater Mohali Area Development Authority v. Manju Jain; it also referred to Order XIV and Order VIII Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
members.conclusion: The appellant could not rely on the unpleaded, fact-dependent agency ground; a new ground involving a pure question of law that requires no inquiry or proof may be raised at any stage.

predicates.appellate_proceeding: A party seeks to advance a ground in an appeal or other appellate proceeding.
predicates.new_ground_requires_factual_inquiry: The proposed ground depends on factual matters that would require evidence or factual inquiry.
predicates.factual_basis_not_pleaded: The party did not set out the material factual basis for the ground in its pleadings.

members.legal_issue: A Letters Patent appellate bench hearing an appeal from a second appeal cannot itself resolve new disputed factual issues that require additional evidence and fresh fact-finding.
material_facts: The Letters Patent appeal arose from a judgment disposing of a second appeal.
After the pleadings were amended, new disputed issues arose about the landlord's need for the premises and the availability of suitable accommodation.
The appellate bench permitted oral and documentary evidence, assessed it, and made factual findings on those issues.
The amended issues required fresh fact-finding that had not been undertaken by the trial court or the first appellate court.
members.legal_principle: Sections 100 and 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure limit a High Court's role in a second appeal: its power to determine facts is confined to specified circumstances and to evidence on the record. An appeal under Clause 15 of the Letters Patent from a decision in second appeal is subject to those same limits. Order 41, Rule 27 concerns admission of additional evidence and does not authorize the appellate court to undertake fresh trial-level assessment of disputed facts. The Court distinguished admitting evidence from appreciating it and acting on it, and held Indrajit Pratap Sahi v. Amar Singh, 50 I.A. 183, and Surinder Kumar v. Gian Chand, [1958] S.C.R. 548, inapplicable to that question.
members.conclusion: The appellate bench could not take and assess the new evidence and make findings on the fresh disputed factual issues; the matter had to be remanded for fact-finding by the appropriate lower court.

predicates.letters_patent_appeal_from_second_appeal: A Letters Patent appeal was brought from a judgment disposing of a second appeal.
predicates.amended_pleadings_created_new_disputed_f: Amended pleadings introduced factual disputes that had not previously been part of the case.
predicates.additional_evidence_needed_for_fresh_fac: Resolving the new factual disputes required additional evidence and its assessment.

members.legal_issue: A challenge to a plaintiff's standing based on an alleged relinquishment cannot be raised for the first time at a late appellate stage when it was not disputed or preserved earlier.
material_facts: The defendants raised the contention that the plaintiff had relinquished her rights in favour of her sons and therefore lacked standing.
The plaint had alleged that the relinquishment was inoperative and void.
The defendants did not dispute that allegation in the earlier proceedings and did not raise the contention at the proper stages or in their grounds of appeal.
members.legal_principle: A party cannot raise at a late appellate stage a contention that could have been raised earlier but was not; where the opposing party's pleading stated that the relinquishment was inoperative and the allegation was not disputed, the opposing party may also have been deprived of the opportunity to prove that it had ceased to operate or to amend the pleading.
members.conclusion: The defendants could not raise the standing contention at that stage, and the contention was rejected.

rule.if: estate_recovery_appeal and standing_challenge_based_on_relinquishment and relinquishment_invalidity_pleaded and challenge_not_preserved_earlier

predicates.estate_recovery_appeal: An appeal arises from a suit seeking recovery of an estate.
predicates.standing_challenge_based_on_relinquishme: A party argues that the plaintiff lacks standing because she relinquished her rights to others.
predicates.relinquishment_invalidity_pleaded: The plaintiff pleaded that the alleged relinquishment was inoperative or void.
predicates.challenge_not_preserved_earlier: The opposing party did not dispute that pleading or raise the standing challenge at the proper earlier stages.

members.legal_issue: A tenant cannot take a position contrary to a final finding between the same parties in an earlier rent-control proceeding when principles analogous to res judicata apply.
material_facts: The society applied under section 44 of the Delhi Rent Control Act for permission to make repairs.
The Rent Controller found that the society was tenant only of an open site and that the shed had been constructed by the society.
That finding became final between the parties.
In the later possession proceedings, the society sought to contend that the property was premises covered by the Act.
members.legal_principle: A final finding between the same parties may, on principles analogous to res judicata, prevent a party from taking a contrary position in later proceedings. The Court applied that principle to the Rent Controller’s finding in the society’s application under section 44 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958.
members.conclusion: The society could not take a contrary position in the later proceedings because the Rent Controller’s finding had attained finality between the parties and principles analogous to res judicata applied.

rule.if: later_proceeding_between_same_parties and earlier_rent_control_finding and earlier_finding_became_final and party_takes_contrary_position

predicates.later_proceeding_between_same_parties: A later proceeding is brought between parties who were also parties to an earlier proceeding.
predicates.earlier_rent_control_finding: A rent-control adjudicator made a finding about the nature of the tenancy in an earlier proceeding.
predicates.earlier_finding_became_final: The earlier finding became final between the parties.
predicates.party_takes_contrary_position: A party in the later proceeding advances a position inconsistent with the earlier finding.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot rely at the appellate stage on a new defence that was not raised or adjudicated at trial.
material_facts: The director did not plead a licence or its irrevocability in the trial court, and that issue was not adjudicated there.
The director first raised the statutory licence argument in the appeal and relied on it before the Supreme Court.
members.legal_principle: A party may not change its case at the appellate stage by introducing a defence that was not raised and adjudicated in the trial court.
members.conclusion: The director could not change the case at the appellate stage by raising a licence defence that had not been pleaded or adjudicated at trial.

rule.if: civil_appeal and defence_not_raised_at_trial and defence_not_adjudicated_at_trial and new_defence_introduced_on_appeal

predicates.civil_appeal: A party pursued an appeal in a civil case.
predicates.defence_not_raised_at_trial: The party did not plead the defence before the trial court.
predicates.defence_not_adjudicated_at_trial: The trial court did not decide the defence.
predicates.new_defence_introduced_on_appeal: The party relied on the previously unraised defence in the appeal.

members.legal_issue: A fact-dependent challenge to the validity of an arbitration agreement cannot be raised for the first time at an appellate or appeal-certificate stage when it was not founded in the pleadings.
material_facts: The parties referred the compensation dispute to an arbitration board, and the appellant participated in the arbitration proceedings.

The appellant treated the government resolution as a valid arbitration agreement and did not challenge its validity in the pleadings or at the hearing before the trial court or during the appeal on its merits.
After the arbitration award confirmed the compensation, the appellant first challenged the agreement's validity in an application for a certificate to appeal.
Determining whether the agreement met the required formalities depended on investigation of facts, and the opposing party could have presented evidence if the issue had been raised earlier.
members.legal_principle: Under Order VI Rule 8 and Order VIII Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an issue requiring factual investigation must have a foundation in the pleadings; evidence cannot be considered on an issue not pleaded. Applying Kalyanpur Lime Works Ltd. v. State of Bihar, the Court held that a party may not raise such a point for the first time at an appellate stage. The Court did not decide whether the arbitration agreement in fact complied with Article 299 of the Constitution.
members.conclusion: The appellant could not raise the fact-dependent challenge for the first time before the Supreme Court, and the High Court should not have entertained it at the certificate application stage.

rule.if: appellate_challenge_to_arbitration_award and fact_dependent_validity_plea and plea_omitted_from_earlier_pleadings and plea_first_raised_at_late_appellate_stage and party_participated_in_arbitration

predicates.appellate_challenge_to_arbitration_award: A party brings an appellate challenge concerning an award made in an arbitration proceeding.
predicates.fact_dependent_validity_plea: The party's challenge to the arbitration agreement's validity depends on investigation of facts.
predicates.plea_omitted_from_earlier_pleadings: The party did not include the validity challenge in the pleadings before the original decision-maker.
predicates.plea_first_raised_at_late_appellate_stag: The party first raises the validity challenge at a later appellate stage, rather than during the original hearing or an appeal on its merits.
predicates.party_participated_in_arbitration: The party participated in the arbitration proceeding under the agreement it later challenged.
predicates.late_fact_dependent_plea_not_entertained: The fact-dependent validity challenge is not entertained when first raised at the late appellate stage.

members.legal_issue: A claim that another country’s title was lost through adverse possession cannot be introduced for the first time on appeal when the governments involved do not claim adverse possession, and the court need not decide the claim’s merits.
material_facts: The appellants raised adverse possession only during the appeal and conceded that the plea had not been made in the writ petition.
The Union and the State respondents did not claim that their possession was adverse; they maintained that the territory belonged to Pakistan and should be delivered to it.
members.legal_principle: A contention not raised in the original writ petition could not be introduced in the appeal in the circumstances of this case, particularly where the governmental parties whose possession was invoked expressly disclaimed any claim of adverse possession. The Court therefore did not reach the international-law or evidentiary merits.
members.conclusion: The adverse-possession contention was not entertained, and the Court found it unnecessary to decide whether such a claim could be made under international law or whether the evidence would support it.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_dismissal: The proceeding is an appeal from the dismissal of a writ petition.
predicates.adverse_possession_claim_first_raised_on: A party first raises an adverse-possession claim during the appeal, not in the original petition.
predicates.government_parties_disclaim_adverse_clai: The government parties whose possession is relied on do not assert that their possession was adverse.

members.legal_issue: A claim of acquisition of title by adverse possession cannot be raised for the first time at the appellate stage when it was not an issue at trial.
material_facts: There was no trial issue about whether the deity had acquired title to the lands by adverse possession.
The plaintiffs sought to raise that claim at the appellate stage.
The plaintiffs did not establish that the deity had acquired title to any part of the lands by adverse possession.
members.legal_principle: A plea of acquisition of title by adverse possession cannot be raised for the first time at the appellate stage when no issue on it was tried below.
members.conclusion: The plaintiffs could not raise the adverse-possession claim for the first time on appeal and failed to establish acquisition of title by adverse possession.

predicates.civil_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a civil suit.
predicates.no_trial_issue_on_adverse_possession: The trial did not include an issue about acquisition of title by adverse possession.
predicates.adverse_possession_plea_raised_first_on_: The claimant raised the adverse-possession plea for the first time in the appeal.
predicates.adverse_possession_plea_cannot_be_raised: The adverse-possession plea cannot be raised for the first time at the appellate stage.

members.legal_issue: A civil appellate court cannot decide a claim or defence on a factual ground that was not pleaded.
material_facts: Both defendants pleaded that a partition had occurred and disputed which brother received the properties; neither pleaded that the properties remained joint family property because no partition had occurred.

The second defendant denied executing the agreement and pleaded forgery, but did not plead misrepresentation; the first appellate court nevertheless found that the agreement had been obtained by misrepresentation.
members.legal_principle: A case not pleaded cannot be made out by evidence, and a court cannot decide the validity of a document on an unpleaded defence. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this principle.
members.conclusion: The first appellate court could not find that the properties remained joint family property or invalidate the agreement for misrepresentation when those grounds were not pleaded. The High Court was justified in reversing the first finding.

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal involving findings made by a lower appellate court.
predicates.joint_family_case_absent_from_pleadings: The parties pleaded a partition and disputed the allocation of property, but no party pleaded that the property remained jointly owned because there had been no partition.
predicates.misrepresentation_defence_absent_from_pl: The party denying a document's execution pleaded forgery but did not plead that the document was obtained by misrepresentation.

members.legal_issue: A party that pleads a challenge to a property transfer in its first suit must seek the corresponding relief in that suit and cannot reserve the challenge for later litigation.
material_facts: In a suit seeking recognition of leasehold rights and protection of possession, the tenants pleaded that the transfer of the property was invalid and that the transferees had no title.

Although the prayer was awkwardly worded and did not expressly seek a separate declaration concerning title, the court found that the pleading and first prayer showed an intention to challenge the transfer.
The tenants sought to raise the transfer and title dispute in later proceedings without appealing the dismissal of the first suit.
members.legal_principle: Order II Rule 2 CPC bars a later suit for relief arising from a cause of action when the plaintiff omitted to claim that relief in the earlier suit, subject to the rule’s requirements. The court held that the pleadings and prayer, read in substance, showed that the tenants sought to assail the transfer; the bar would not apply if they had merely alleged an apprehension of dispossession without challenging the property’s legal character or the transferor’s capacity to convey it.
members.conclusion: Order II Rule 2 CPC barred the tenants from reserving the pleaded challenge to the transfer for a later proceeding.

predicates.first_suit_seeks_possession_protection: A plaintiff brings a first suit seeking recognition of a right to possess property or protection against interference with possession.
predicates.transfer_challenge_pleaded: The plaintiff’s pleadings challenge the validity of a transfer or the transferor’s capacity to make it.
predicates.related_transfer_relief_omitted: The plaintiff does not seek the relief corresponding to that pleaded transfer challenge in the first suit.
predicates.omitted_transfer_relief_barred_later: The plaintiff cannot pursue the omitted transfer-related relief in a later proceeding.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot challenge the validity of a gift for the first time in a final appeal when the challenge has no foundation in the pleadings, issues or evidence.
material_facts: The parties seeking to challenge the gift had not pleaded a challenge to its validity in the suit.
No issue concerning the validity of the gift had been framed.
No evidence had been led to challenge the gift’s validity.
The challenge was raised for the first time in the Supreme Court.
members.legal_principle: A court cannot decide a newly raised challenge to a transaction when no factual foundation for it was laid in the pleadings, no issue was framed, and no evidence was led. The Court did not rely on a specific statutory provision or earlier case for this conclusion.
members.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain the challenge to the gift’s validity for the first time in the appeal.

rule.if: final_appeal and gift_validity_challenged_for_first_time and challenge_not_pleaded and no_issue_framed and no_evidence_supports_challenge

predicates.final_appeal: The proceeding is a final appeal from a lower-court decision.
predicates.gift_validity_challenged_for_first_time: A party first contests the validity of a gift in the final appeal.
predicates.challenge_not_pleaded: The party did not plead the validity challenge in the underlying suit.
predicates.no_issue_framed: The lower court did not frame an issue on the validity challenge.
predicates.no_evidence_supports_challenge: The party led no evidence in the lower court to support the validity challenge.

members.legal_issue: An additional-accommodation ground that was not canvassed before the High Court and was not seriously pressed before the appellate authority cannot support eviction in the appeal.
material_facts: The landlord had originally sought eviction on additional-accommodation and other grounds, as well as on a later-added building-condition ground.
The additional-accommodation ground was not canvassed before the High Court.
The appellate authority observed that the building-condition ground was the only ground seriously pressed; the additional-accommodation point was raised only incidentally.
members.legal_principle: The court declined to rely on the additional-accommodation ground because it had not been canvassed before the High Court and had not been seriously pressed before the appellate authority; the judgment identifies no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this conclusion.
members.conclusion: The landlord’s additional-accommodation contention had no merit in the appeal and did not provide a basis to uphold eviction.

predicates.tenant_eviction_appeal: A tenant appealed against an order directing eviction.
predicates.additional_accommodation_ground_not_canv: The landlord did not argue the additional-accommodation ground before the High Court.
predicates.additional_accommodation_ground_not_seri: The landlord did not seriously press that ground before the lower appellate decision-maker.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot introduce a new factual case for the first time in a writ proceeding when it was not founded before the lower authority and the opposing party is not given an opportunity to answer it.
material_facts: Before the appellate and revisional authorities, the applicant relied on financial difficulties and did not plead that she had not received the allotment letter.
The applicant first alleged non-receipt of the allotment letter in the writ petition.
The High Court relied on that new factual case without giving the authority a proper opportunity to controvert it or produce supporting material.
members.legal_principle: A pure question of law may be raised at any stage, but a factual or mixed question requiring investigation cannot be raised for the first time in a writ petition without a factual foundation before the lower authority. If a court exceptionally entertains such a new factual plea, it must give the opposing party an opportunity to controvert it and adduce evidence. State of U.P. v. Dr. Anupam Gupta; Ram Kumar Agrawal v. Thawar Das; Vasantha Viswanathan v. V.K. Elayalwar; Anup Kumar Kundu v. Sudip Charan Chakraborty; Tirupati Jute Industries (P) Ltd. v. State of West Bengal; Sanghvi Reconditioners (P) Ltd. v. Union of India; and Fuljit Kaur v. State of Punjab.
members.conclusion: The High Court should not have entertained the new factual plea in those circumstances; its haste and failure to provide an opportunity to answer the plea were arbitrary.

predicates.writ_review_of_lower_authority_decision: A court considered a writ petition challenging a decision made by a lower authority.
predicates.factual_plea_first_raised_in_writ: A party first asserted a material factual claim in the writ proceeding, without having raised it before the lower authority.
predicates.opposing_party_given_no_chance_to_answer: The court did not give the opposing party a proper opportunity to respond to the new factual claim and present supporting evidence.

members.legal_issue: A court may refuse to permit an appellant to advance a new statutory basis that was not pursued below and conflicts with the basis on which the appellant consistently relied.
material_facts: The appellant had relied in the lower courts and in the grounds of appeal on principles of justice, equity and good conscience rather than on the statutory provisions applying of their own force.
The appellant advanced the new statutory contention for the first time in the Supreme Court.
The court had discretion to permit a new point but declined to exercise it in these circumstances.
members.legal_principle: Although an appeal admitted by certificate is before the court in its full scope, the court retains discretion to refuse a new point. The court applied that discretion because the appellant had not advanced the statutory theory below and had consistently relied on a different legal basis.
members.conclusion: The court refused to permit the appellant to shift to the new statutory contention and decided the matter on the basis the appellant had previously maintained.

predicates.certificate_appeal: The case is an appeal admitted by certificate.
predicates.new_statutory_point_not_raised_below: The appellant did not advance the statutory argument in the courts below.
predicates.appellant_consistently_relied_on_differe: The appellant consistently relied on a different legal basis in the courts below and in the appeal grounds.
predicates.court_may_refuse_new_point: The court may decline to allow the appellant to advance the new point.

members.legal_issue: A second appellate court cannot find that a party’s property title was extinguished by adverse possession when that issue was not raised in the courts below.
material_facts: The courts below found that the plaintiff had not proved the claimed long-term possession and that he had trespassed onto the land in 1967.
No issue of adverse possession had been raised in the courts below.
The second appellate court concluded for the first time that the institution’s title had been extinguished by adverse possession.
The evidence accepted by the courts below supported the institution’s possession after it obtained delivery of the land and until the plaintiff’s trespass.
members.legal_principle: Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a second appellate court cannot make a new factual determination by deciding an issue that was not raised in the courts below. The finding of adverse possession also lacked support in the possession findings accepted by those courts.
members.conclusion: The second appellate court’s finding that the institution’s title was extinguished was unsupportable and was set aside; the institution’s title had not been extinguished.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding is a second appeal.
predicates.adverse_possession_issue_not_raised_belo: The parties did not raise adverse possession as an issue in the courts below.
predicates.second_appellate_court_finds_title_extin: The court hearing the second appeal finds that a party’s title was extinguished through another party’s adverse possession.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot raise for the first time on appeal a challenge to the opposing party’s status as the next reversionary heirs when the trial proceeded on the contrary footing and no issue on that status was tried.
material_facts: The appellants contended on appeal that a son of one claimant was the reversionary heir.
No issue about the claimants’ status as the next reversioners had been raised at trial, and the trial proceeded on the footing that they held that status.
The trial court refused the appellants leave to file an additional statement raising the issue.
The record did not establish that the alleged son was alive when the limited heir died.
members.legal_principle: The Court relied on the way the case had been pleaded and tried: the claimants’ status as next reversioners was assumed at trial, no issue on that question was raised, and leave to raise it later was refused. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this issue.
members.conclusion: The appellants could not contend on appeal that the claimants were not the reversionary heirs entitled to succeed to the estate.

predicates.civil_appeal_challenges_reversionary_sta: The proceeding is a civil appeal in which a party challenges the opposing claimants’ status as reversionary heirs.
predicates.trial_proceeded_on_claimants_being_next_: The trial proceeded on the footing that the claimants were the next reversioners.
predicates.no_trial_issue_on_reversionary_status: No issue about the claimants’ reversionary status was raised for trial.
predicates.leave_to_raise_issue_later_was_refused: The trial court refused permission to add the reversionary-status issue later.

members.legal_issue: A plea of mala fides that was not raised and supported by evidence at trial cannot be introduced for the first time on appeal.
material_facts: The accused argued at the appellate stage that the by-law had been made out of spite and enmity.
No appropriate allegations of mala fides had been made at trial, and no evidence had been led there to prove the plea.
members.legal_principle: A party alleging mala fides must make appropriate allegations at trial and lead evidence to prove them; the plea cannot be raised for the first time on appeal.
members.conclusion: The Court did not permit the plea of mala fides to be raised for the first time on appeal.

predicates.appeal_after_trial: The claim is made in an appeal following a trial.
predicates.malafides_claim_first_raised_on_appeal: A party first alleges at the appellate stage that an act was done out of spite or improper motive.
predicates.no_trial_allegations_or_evidence: The party made no appropriate trial allegations and led no trial evidence to establish the alleged improper motive.

members.legal_issue: A party’s new challenge to the validity of an allotment is not considered when that ground was not raised in its statement of case.
material_facts: The respondents argued that the appellants’ allotment was itself invalid because an earlier cancellation had contravened the governing rule.
The respondents had not raised that ground in their statement of case, so the appellants had not been given the opportunity to answer it.
members.legal_principle: A new ground not raised in the statement of case need not be considered where the opposing party was not given the opportunity to answer it.
members.conclusion: The Court declined to consider the new ground.

predicates.supreme_court_appeal: The matter is before the Supreme Court on appeal.
predicates.challenge_ground_not_raised_in_statement: A party advances a challenge ground that it did not raise in its statement of case.
predicates.opposing_party_lacked_opportunity_to_ans: The opposing party was not given an opportunity to provide an answer to that ground.

members.legal_issue: An appellate court may not dismiss a suit on a statutory ground raised for the first time on appeal when the ground was not pleaded or tried and its effect depends on uncertain future events.
material_facts: The High Court relied on a land-reform ground that had not been raised in the written statement, had not been made the subject of a trial issue, and did not appear to have been argued before the trial court.
The widow remained alive, and the plaintiffs sought no possession; the effect of setting aside the settlements on future rights in the property was uncertain.
The High Court relied on the land-reform ground to conclude that granting relief in the suit would serve no purpose.
members.legal_principle: A ground not raised in the pleadings or tried as an issue should not be entertained for the first time in appeal where its factual and legal consequences have not been determined. The Court applied this principle to the proposed reliance on Section 6 of the Bihar Land Reforms Act and declined to speculate about rights dependent on future events.
members.conclusion: The High Court erred in relying on the land-reform ground at that stage. The Court did not decide whether the transferees would ultimately be entitled to an interest in the property under that law.

rule.if: appeal_from_suit_decree and statutory_ground_first_raised_on_appeal and ground_not_pleaded and no_trial_issue_on_ground and future_property_effect_uncertain

predicates.appeal_from_suit_decree: A party appealed from a decree entered in a suit.
predicates.statutory_ground_first_raised_on_appeal: A party relied on a statutory ground for the first time during the appeal.
predicates.ground_not_pleaded: The party had not raised that ground in the pleadings.
predicates.no_trial_issue_on_ground: The trial court had not framed or decided an issue on that ground.
predicates.future_property_effect_uncertain: The effect of the ground depended on property rights that could not yet be determined.

members.legal_issue: A party may not advance on appeal a contention that contradicts the position it took in its original pleading.
material_facts: In its writ petition, the company asserted that it was the lessee of the government-owned land.
On appeal, counsel argued that the company was not a lessee and that no lease existed in its favour.
members.legal_principle: The Court treated a submission contrary to the party’s own pleaded case as impermissible and declined to consider it.
members.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain the contention because it contradicted the company’s case in its writ petition.

predicates.appeal_from_challenged_demand: A party appeals in a proceeding concerning a challenged assessment demand.
predicates.appellate_argument_contradicts_original_: The party advances an appellate contention that contradicts its position in its original pleading.

members.legal_issue: An appellate court will not entertain a new plea requiring further evidence when it is raised for the first time on appeal and the opposing party had no opportunity to meet it.
material_facts: The landlord argued for the first time before the Supreme Court that the tenant should not be allowed to claim that the tenancy covered professional as well as residential use because he had previously obtained extensions by describing it as residential.
The plea required relevant evidence, and the tenant had no opportunity to meet it because it had not been raised at the proper stage.
The parties’ earlier conduct included positions inconsistent with the positions they later advanced.
members.legal_principle: The Court applied the settled practice that new pleas requiring further evidence are not allowed in appeals under Article 136 of the Constitution, particularly where the opposing party had no opportunity to respond. No earlier cases were cited.
members.conclusion: The landlord could not raise the new plea in the appeal.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and new_plea_raised_first_time and plea_requires_further_evidence and opposing_party_lacked_opportunity

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The matter is an appeal brought by special leave.
predicates.new_plea_raised_first_time: A party advances the plea for the first time in the appellate court.
predicates.plea_requires_further_evidence: Determining the plea requires evidence beyond the record already made.
predicates.opposing_party_lacked_opportunity: The opposing party had no opportunity at the proper stage to meet the plea.

members.legal_issue: A court may not decide a challenge that a gift was fraudulent or backdated when the challenge was not pleaded and the parties did not try the case on that issue.
material_facts: The written statement challenged the transfer and alleged collusion in bringing the suit, but did not allege that the gift was fraudulent or had been executed after the later sale.
No issue was framed on fraud or backdating, and no evidence was led with notice that either allegation would be decided.
The appellate court inferred backdating from a delay in registration and the non-production of a petition-writer’s register, although the respondents were not responsible for producing that register.
members.legal_principle: A decision may address an unpleaded matter where the parties went to trial knowing it was in issue and adduced evidence on it, but not where the opposing party lacked notice and an opportunity to meet the case. The Court distinguished Kidar Lall Seal v. Hari Lall Seal, Nagubai Ammal v. B. Shama Rao, Kunju Kasavan v. M.M. Philip, and Union of India v. Khas Karanapura Colliery Ltd. It also held that a presumption could not be drawn against the respondents from the petition-writer’s failure to produce a register that they neither maintained nor possessed.
members.conclusion: The High Court was right to set aside the findings of fraud and backdating because those matters had not been pleaded or tried, and the backdating finding lacked evidentiary support.

predicates.civil_property_title_suit: The proceeding was a civil suit seeking a determination of title to property.
predicates.challenged_transfer_was_not_pleaded_as_f: The party challenging the transfer did not plead that it was fraudulent or backdated.
predicates.parties_did_not_try_that_issue_with_noti: The parties did not proceed with notice that fraud or backdating was in issue or present evidence directed to that issue.

members.legal_issue: A person claiming ownership through adverse possession cannot obtain a declaration of ownership by bringing a suit on that basis.
material_facts: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking a declaration that it had become owner through adverse possession.
The trial court found that the plaintiff had been in adverse possession, but denied the declaration; the appellate courts also denied that relief.
members.legal_principle: Adverse possession may be used as a shield and not as a sword: a person claiming adverse possession may plead it in defence but cannot use it as the basis for a suit seeking a declaration of ownership. The Court affirmed the principle applied in Gurudwara Sahib Sannauli v. State of Punjab, PLR 756. No statutory provision is identified in the judgment.
members.conclusion: A declaration that ownership has matured through adverse possession cannot be sought by the person claiming adverse possession as plaintiff; adverse possession is available to that person only as a defence when proceedings are brought against them.

predicates.plaintiff_seeks_ownership_declaration: The claimant brings a suit seeking a declaration that the claimant owns the property.
predicates.claim_based_on_adverse_possession: The claimant bases the asserted ownership on having possessed the property adversely.

members.legal_issue: An appellate court cannot reverse a trial court’s decision by relying on a case that was neither pleaded nor made an issue between the parties.
material_facts: The plaintiffs pleaded that the deceased owned the restaurant and had employed the defendant, and that the defendant received possession on an assurance that he would manage it for them.
The defendant pleaded that he had always owned the restaurant.
The plaintiffs did not plead that the restaurant was a benami business, and the parties did not join issue on that theory.
The High Court reversed the trial court’s decision for the defendant on the basis that the restaurant was benami for the deceased.
members.legal_principle: A case must be decided on the case pleaded by the parties, and a decision cannot rest on grounds outside their pleadings. The Court relied on Trejan and Co. Ltd. v. P.W. N.H. Nagappa Chettiar (1956) SCR 789 and Baraba Singh v. Achal Singh, AIR 1961 SC 1097.
members.conclusion: The High Court’s judgment and decree were set aside, and the trial court’s decree was restored.

rule.if: civil_appeal and appellate_court_reversed_trial_decree and appellate_court_relied_on_unpleaded_case and parties_did_not_join_issue_on_that_case

predicates.civil_appeal: A party brought a civil appeal challenging a decision made by a trial court.
predicates.appellate_court_reversed_trial_decree: The appellate court reversed the trial court’s decree.
predicates.appellate_court_relied_on_unpleaded_case: The appellate court relied on a factual or legal case that was not pleaded by the parties.
predicates.parties_did_not_join_issue_on_that_case: The parties did not make the unpleaded case an issue for decision in the proceedings.

members.legal_issue: A second appellate court cannot introduce a new factual theory that was not pleaded or supported by an issue and evidence below.
material_facts: In the second appeal, the High Court treated the sale as having arisen from a new agreement between the receiver and the creditor, and found that the earlier agreement had been breached.
The breach issue had not been pressed at trial, no issue or evidence supported a new agreement, and the creditor testified that there had been no fresh agreement.
members.legal_principle: Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not permit a new factual case to be made for the first time in second appeal when it was not raised through an issue or supported by evidence. Novation under section 62 of the Contract Act requires a clear plea, issue and evidence.
members.conclusion: The High Court exceeded its jurisdiction in second appeal by making those findings, and the findings were set aside.

rule.if: second_appeal and (issue_not_pressed_below or no_issue_on_new_theory) and no_evidence_for_new_theory

predicates.second_appeal: The matter is before a court exercising second appellate jurisdiction.
predicates.issue_not_pressed_below: The issue on which the new finding rests was not pressed in the trial court.
predicates.no_issue_on_new_theory: No issue was framed on the new factual theory.
predicates.no_evidence_for_new_theory: The record contains no evidence supporting the new factual theory.

members.legal_issue: A challenge to a state property transfer cannot be expanded on appeal where the factual basis for alleged arbitrariness was not pleaded in the original writ proceeding.
material_facts: The original writ petition did not plead a factual basis for the later claim that the transfer was arbitrary, including allegations about the absence of an advertisement, auction, or tender.
The arbitrariness argument was advanced in the appeal and before the Supreme Court without supporting pleadings in the original proceeding.
The alleged circumstances required a response from the State, which had not been given an opportunity to address them on properly pleaded facts.
members.legal_principle: A party challenging executive action must plead the material facts supporting the challenge so the State can answer them. An appeal continuing an original writ proceeding does not ordinarily enlarge its scope. The Court relied on the general requirement that executive action be fair and non-arbitrary, including the principles in A.S. Ahluwalia v. State of Punjab, Sukhdev Singh v. Bhagatram Sardar Singh Raghuvanshi, and Ramana Dayaram Shetty v. International Airport Authority of India.
members.conclusion: The appellate proceedings could not enlarge the inquiry beyond the original writ petition, and the Court declined to entertain the unsupported arbitrariness challenge.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_state_property_transfe: A person brings a writ proceeding challenging the transfer or disposition of state property.
predicates.material_facts_for_arbitrariness_not_ple: The challenger does not plead the material circumstances said to make the state's action arbitrary.
predicates.arbitrariness_basis_raised_only_later: The challenger first advances the factual basis for arbitrariness during a later appeal or proceeding.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot challenge an adoption’s validity on a ground that was not pleaded when the issue was not tried and the parties had no opportunity to lead evidence on it.
material_facts: The defendants did not plead that the adoptive father lacked power to adopt the adopted person because he was the adoptive father’s daughter’s son.
The validity of the adoption was therefore not in issue, and the parties had no opportunity to lead evidence on that question.
members.legal_principle: A ground that was not pleaded and was not put in issue cannot be raised where the parties consequently had no opportunity to adduce evidence on it. The judgment cited no earlier case or statutory provision for this ruling.
members.conclusion: The defendants could not challenge the validity of the adoption on that ground.

predicates.adoption_succession_dispute: The parties are litigating succession in reliance on an adoption.
predicates.invalidity_ground_not_pleaded: The party challenging the adoption did not plead the ground on which it later seeks to dispute the adoption’s validity.
predicates.no_opportunity_to_lead_evidence_on_valid: Because the validity ground was not in issue, the parties had no opportunity to lead evidence on it.

members.legal_issue: An appellate court may not overturn an eviction decree solely on a title objection that was not pleaded or tried, and must decide the appeal on the pleadings and merits.
material_facts: The tenant did not dispute the landlord’s title or ownership in the written statement or at trial.
No issue concerning ownership was framed at trial.
The first appellate court raised the ownership question and reversed the eviction decree solely on that basis without examining the reasonable-requirement claim.
The High Court affirmed that decision without examining the merits of the eviction claim.
members.legal_principle: A case is to be decided on the pleadings; where title was not challenged and no issue on ownership was framed, the appellate courts could not set aside the decree solely on that unraised question. The Supreme Court set aside those judgments and remanded the appeal for consideration on its merits. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this procedural ruling.
members.conclusion: The appellate judgments were set aside and the case was remanded for fresh disposal of the tenant’s appeal on the merits, on the basis that the landlord was the owner as pleaded.

rule.if: appeal_from_eviction_decree and tenant_did_not_dispute_title_at_trial and no_ownership_issue_framed and appellate_court_reversed_solely_on_title

predicates.appeal_from_eviction_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree granting eviction.
predicates.tenant_did_not_dispute_title_at_trial: The tenant did not challenge the landlord’s title in the pleadings or at trial.
predicates.no_ownership_issue_framed: The trial court did not frame an issue about the landlord’s ownership.
predicates.appellate_court_reversed_solely_on_title: The appellate court overturned the decree based only on the landlord’s title without deciding the eviction claim on its merits.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot introduce for the first time at the appellate stage an unpleaded distinction between rent and land revenue when that distinction was not raised or tried below and the record treated the terms as including one another.
material_facts: The government’s resolution provided that no rent would be charged for the land.

The recipient asserted before the assessment dispute reached the Supreme Court that rent, in the relevant official usage, included land revenue, and the government did not deny that assertion in its reply.
The government did not plead the distinction between rent and land revenue, the distinction was not made an issue at trial, and it was not advanced in the courts below.
members.legal_principle: An appellate party may not introduce a new contention that was not pleaded, made an issue, or raised in the courts below. Because the assertion that rent included land revenue was not denied in the record, the court proceeded on that basis for this case.
members.conclusion: The government could not raise the distinction at that stage; for deciding the case, rent was treated as synonymous with or including land revenue.

rule.if: assessment_appeal and rent_revenue_distinction_not_pleaded and rent_revenue_distinction_not_tried_below and record_does_not_deny_rent_includes_revenue

predicates.assessment_appeal: An appeal concerns a government assessment imposed on land.
predicates.rent_revenue_distinction_not_pleaded: The party seeking to distinguish rent from land revenue did not raise that distinction in its pleadings.
predicates.rent_revenue_distinction_not_tried_below: The distinction was not made an issue or argued before the lower courts.
predicates.record_does_not_deny_rent_includes_reven: The record contains an assertion that rent includes land revenue that the opposing party did not deny.

members.legal_issue: An unreasoned arbitral award is not invalid per se, and a special leave appeal should not be postponed to await a larger bench when the challenge is raised for the first time at that stage in an old dispute.
material_facts: The award gave no reasons.

The objection that the award was invalid for lack of reasons had not been raised before the trial court, the High Court, or in the original objections to the award; it was raised for the first time in the special leave petition.
The dispute and adjudication were old, and the appellant sought to await a pending larger-bench decision on the validity of unreasoned awards.
members.legal_principle: As the law then stood, an award without reasons was not bad per se and could be set aside only for misconduct or an error of law apparent on its face. In exercising its discretion under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Court would not prolong or unsettle an old arbitration merely because a larger bench was considering the issue, particularly where the objection was raised for the first time in the special leave proceedings.
members.conclusion: The Court refused to postpone the appeal and rejected the contention that the award was invalid merely because it gave no reasons.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal_reviewing_an_arbitral_award and award_gives_no_reasons and challenge_first_raised_in_special_leave_proceedings and dispute_is_old and request_to_await_larger_bench_decision

predicates.special_leave_appeal_reviewing_an_arbitr: A party seeks special leave to challenge a court decision concerning an arbitral award.
predicates.award_gives_no_reasons: The arbitrator issued an award without stating reasons.
predicates.challenge_first_raised_in_special_leave_: The party first objected to the absence of reasons in the special leave proceedings, rather than in the earlier objections or courts.
predicates.dispute_is_old: The arbitration dispute and its adjudication had already become old.
predicates.request_to_await_larger_bench_decision: The party asked the Court to defer deciding the appeal until a larger bench decided the general issue of unreasoned awards.

members.legal_issue: A challenge that the person discharging a prior mortgage did not intend to preserve its priority cannot be raised for the first time on appeal when that factual issue was not pleaded.
material_facts: The mortgagee's representatives pleaded in the trial court that they were entitled to subrogation after discharging the earlier mortgages.
The appellant's trial objection was that subrogation required a written agreement, and no issue or evidence was directed to contrary intention.
The appellant did not raise the contention that the mortgagee intended not to preserve the discharged mortgages before the High Court or in the statement of case in the Supreme Court.
members.legal_principle: Whether a person who discharges a prior encumbrance intended to obtain its priority is a question of fact assessed on the circumstances as a whole. A party disputing that intention must raise it by proper pleading so that an issue can be framed and evidence led. The Court referred to Gokuldass Gopaldass v. Ram Bux Scochand for the approach that, absent contrary evidence, a person is ordinarily presumed to act in their own interest.
members.conclusion: The appellant could not raise the factual contention about contrary intention at that stage, and the claim to subrogation stood established on the pleadings.

predicates.a_subrogation_dispute_is_under_appeal: A civil appeal concerns a claim to subrogation after a prior mortgage has been discharged.
predicates.the_claimant_pleaded_entitlement_to_subr: The person claiming subrogation alleged in the trial court that the circumstances of the discharge entitled them to that relief.
predicates.contrary_intention_was_not_pleaded: The opposing party did not plead that the person discharging the mortgage intended not to preserve its priority.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot rely after the hearing on a policy that was not raised or relied on during the proceedings to establish an entitlement that was never previously advanced.
material_facts: After the hearing had concluded, the respondent applied for directions seeking to rely on a government policy.
The policy had not been referred to or relied on at any earlier stage, and no earlier submission had addressed the respondent’s entitlement under it.
The Supreme Court rejected the application for directions.
members.legal_principle: The Court declined to entertain reliance on material introduced after the hearing where that material had not previously been raised or relied on and no earlier submission had established the claimed entitlement. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.
members.conclusion: The application for directions was rejected.

predicates.application_made_after_conclusion_of_hea: A party makes an application after the court has concluded hearing the matter.
predicates.seeks_to_rely_on_policy_not_previously_r: The application seeks to rely on a policy that was not previously referred to or relied on in the proceedings.
predicates.no_prior_submission_established_entitlem: No submission made before the hearing concluded established the party’s claimed entitlement under that policy.

members.legal_issue: An appellant may not replace the case presented in the courts below with a materially different factual theory on appeal.
material_facts: The appellant’s case in the courts below was that the partner took the sub-lease as a benamidar for the partnership firm.
In the Supreme Court, the appellant relied on the firm’s possession of the colliery to argue that the partnership had already existed when the sub-lease was obtained, a case not previously advanced.
members.legal_principle: The Court held that it would not be proper to permit an appellant to advance an entirely new case at the appellate stage when the opposing parties had been required to meet a different case in the courts below.
members.conclusion: The Court would not permit the appellant to make out the new case on appeal.

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal.
predicates.new_factual_theory_not_advanced_below: The appellant relies on a materially different factual theory from the one presented in the courts below.
predicates.appellate_court_does_not_allow_new_case: The appellate court does not permit the appellant to make out the new case.

members.legal_issue: A factual defense raised for the first time in a special-leave appeal cannot be entertained when it is inconsistent with the pleadings and would prejudice the opposing party by depriving them of an opportunity to rebut it.
material_facts: The tenants had pleaded that the tenant remained in possession of the entire shop, but first argued in the special-leave petition that his sons occupied a portion exclusively with his permission.
The permission argument had not been raised in the written statement or pressed before the lower authorities.
The landlord had no opportunity to contest the new factual claim.
members.legal_principle: A new plea of fact, unlike a plea of law, should not be entertained when it was not pleaded or pursued below, is inconsistent with the existing case, and the opposing party had no opportunity to rebut it. No earlier cases or specific statutory provisions are cited for this principle.
members.conclusion: The tenants were not permitted to raise the new factual plea in the appeal.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and new_factual_plea and inconsistent_with_earlier_pleading and not raised_below and opposing_party_lacked_opportunity_to_rebut

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The case is a special-leave appeal.
predicates.new_factual_plea: A party advances a factual defense that was not part of its earlier case.
predicates.inconsistent_with_earlier_pleading: The new factual defense conflicts with the party's earlier pleading.
predicates.raised_below: The party raised the factual defense before the lower decision-makers.
predicates.opposing_party_lacked_opportunity_to_reb: The opposing party had no opportunity to contest the new factual defense.

members.legal_issue: A party that denied the existence of a contract without pleading its legal unenforceability cannot raise a new, fact-dependent objection to enforceability for the first time in argument when the opposing party lacked an opportunity to meet it.
material_facts: The Government’s pleadings disputed whether a concluded contract had been made but did not plead that the contract was unenforceable for failure to comply with the required manner of execution.
The objection was raised for the first time during argument in the High Court.
Determining whether the Government’s authorised officer had signed the relevant lease documents required factual investigation.
The company had sought production of the documents, but the Government did not produce all of them, and the company had no opportunity at trial to present evidence addressing the objection.
members.legal_principle: Order VI, rule 8 of the Civil Procedure Code provides that a bare denial of an alleged contract is a denial of fact, not a denial of its legality or legal sufficiency. Order VIII, rule 2 requires a defendant to plead matters showing that a transaction is void or unenforceable, including grounds that would take the other party by surprise or raise factual issues not arising from the plaint.
members.conclusion: The High Court should not have allowed the objection to be raised at the argument stage. The Court rejected the objection on that procedural ground without deciding whether the contract had in fact been executed in the required manner.

rule.if: contract_enforcement_suit and contract_denied_only_as_a_fact and unenforceability_not_pleaded and defense_requires_factual_inquiry and opposing_party_lacked_opportunity_to_meet_defense

predicates.contract_enforcement_suit: A claimant seeks enforcement of an alleged contract.
predicates.contract_denied_only_as_a_fact: The opposing party’s pleadings deny that the contract was made but do not challenge its legal enforceability.
predicates.unenforceability_not_pleaded: The opposing party did not plead the legal ground later relied on to resist enforcement.
predicates.defense_requires_factual_inquiry: Deciding the late defense would require investigation of facts.
predicates.opposing_party_lacked_opportunity_to_mee: The claimant had no adequate opportunity to present evidence or otherwise address the factual defense.

members.legal_issue: Ownership of property cannot be awarded on the basis of adverse possession when that basis was neither pleaded nor made an issue for trial.
material_facts: The claimant sued for a declaration of ownership and a permanent injunction concerning land.
The trial court found that the claimant had purchased the land and also declared him owner by adverse possession, although he had not pleaded adverse possession and no issue on it had been framed.
The first appellate court found that the claimant had not proved the purchase and set aside the decree; the High Court affirmed that decision.
The Supreme Court endorsed the appellate courts’ findings and held that the trial court’s decree based on adverse possession was erroneous and unsustainable.
members.legal_principle: A claim of adverse possession is a blended question of fact and law and requires proper pleading and proof; a prayer or finding cannot substitute for a plea identifying when possession became adverse. The Court relied on S.M. Karim v. Bibi Sakina, R. Chandevarappa v. State of Karnataka, D.N. Venkatarayappa v. State of Karnataka, Md. Mohammad Ali v. Jagadish Kalita, and Karnataka Board of Wakf v. Government of India.
members.conclusion: The claimant could not obtain a declaration of ownership on an adverse-possession basis that he had not pleaded and that had not been framed as an issue; the appeal was dismissed.

predicates.civil_appeal_from_title_suit: A party brought a civil appeal arising from a suit seeking a declaration of ownership over property.
predicates.adverse_possession_not_pleaded: The claimant did not plead that the claimant had acquired ownership through adverse possession.
predicates.no_adverse_possession_issue_framed: The trial court did not frame an issue for determination on whether ownership had been acquired through adverse possession.

members.legal_issue: A claim of adverse possession that was not pleaded in the written statement cannot be raised for the first time at the appellate stage.
material_facts: The defendants had not based their written statement on adverse possession.
They sought to rely on their long possession only at the appellate stage.
members.legal_principle: The Court applied the procedural principle that a party cannot introduce at the appellate stage a defence that was not made the basis of its written statement. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this point.
members.conclusion: The adverse-possession claim could not be raised at that stage.

predicates.civil_possession_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a civil claim concerning possession.
predicates.adverse_possession_not_pleaded: The party did not set out adverse possession as a basis of its defence in the written statement.
predicates.adverse_possession_raised_at_appellate_s: The party sought to rely on adverse possession only during the appellate proceedings.

members.legal_issue: A party cannot rely on an alleged estoppel by conduct to defeat a later claim when that estoppel was not pleaded and tried.
material_facts: The decree-holders argued that the earlier compromise created an estoppel against the debtors.
They had not pleaded an estoppel by conduct, and the issue had not been tried on that basis.
There was evidence that some payments had been made under the compromise decree.
members.legal_principle: The court distinguished res judicata or estoppel by judgment from a possible estoppel arising from the parties' conduct. The latter required a plea and trial; the proviso to section 16(iii) of the Madras Agriculturists Relief (Amendment) Act, 1948, separately protected sums already paid or realized from a refund requirement.
members.conclusion: The court did not consider an estoppel by conduct because it had not been pleaded and tried; sums already paid were protected from refund by the statutory proviso.

predicates.later_debt_scaling_proceeding: A later proceeding seeks debt scaling after an earlier decree.
predicates.alleged_estoppel_based_on_party_conduct: A party asserts that the other party's conduct in the earlier dealings prevents the later claim.
predicates.conduct_estoppel_not_pleaded_and_tried: The alleged conduct-based estoppel was neither pleaded as an issue nor tried.

members.legal_issue: A tenant who admitted the area of the tenancy in an affidavit in earlier proceedings cannot later dispute that area in a challenge to mesne profits.
material_facts: In earlier proceedings between the same parties, the tenant filed an affidavit admitting the total covered and open area of the tenanted premises.
